title: IB ESS IA Timeline: Finish Before Winter Break
summary: Follow a realistic IB ESS IA timeline from September to November, with weekly goals for planning, data collection, analysis, drafting, and revision.
body_markdown:
Starting your ESS IA in the **first two weeks of September** gives you a realistic chance of finishing before winter break. Approve the research question by mid-September, complete data collection by mid-October, finish analysis by early November, and submit the final report in late November.


This **IB ESS IA timeline** is a recommended schedule, not an official deadline. Your school sets its own internal dates, which take priority. The plan includes time for unsuccessful trials, poor weather, equipment problems, teacher feedback, and competing coursework.


### What the Current ESS IA Requires


In the current ESS course, first assessed in 2026, the IA is officially called the **individual investigation** . The[official IB ESS subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/university-admission/pdfs/environmental-systems-and-societies-subject-brief-en.pdf) states that students gather and analyze data to answer an individually formulated research question. The written report has a maximum of **3,000 words** .


The investigation is allocated **10 hours** of teaching time and contributes **25% at SL** or **20% at HL** . These are official assessment details, but they do not require you to complete the entire process in 10 consecutive hours. Field access, repeated measurements, data processing, and feedback are safer when spread across several weeks.


The investigation must also address an environmental strategy and tensions between perspectives connected to it. The[IB ESS curriculum update](https://www.ibo.org/university-admission/latest-curriculum-updates/environmental-systems-and-societies-updates/) explains the role of perspectives in environmental and societal outcomes. RevisionDojo’s guide to[what the ESS IA is and how it is marked](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-ess-ia-and-how-is-it-marked-2026-first-assessment) summarizes the six assessment areas.


### September-to-November IB ESS IA Timeline


Dates Main task Target outcome


September 1-7 Explore feasible topics Two or three workable ideas


September 8-14 Refine the question Approved question and provisional strategy


September 15-21 Pilot the method Revised procedure and sampling plan


September 22-October 12 Collect data Complete, organized raw dataset


October 13-19 Process data Calculations, tables, and graphs


October 20-November 2 Analyze results Explained patterns, anomalies, and uncertainty


November 3-9 Conclude and evaluate Evidence-based answer and improvements


November 10-16 Assemble the draft Complete report near or below 3,000 words


November 17-30 Revise and submit Corrected final report


### September: Develop a Workable Investigation


### September 1-14: Test feasibility and gain approval


Begin with an environmental issue, then convert it into something measurable. Instead of studying urban pollution generally, investigate how distance from a road affects particulate deposition on leaves at specified sites. For biodiversity, you might compare plant species richness under two defined land-management conditions.


For each idea, check whether you can access the site, equipment, participants, organisms, or secondary dataset. Confirm that the method is repeatable, sufficient data can be collected by mid-October, and a relevant environmental strategy creates meaningful tensions between perspectives.[ESS IA examples](https://www.revisiondojo.com/coursework-exemplars/ess-new-ia) can show an appropriate level of focus, but should never be copied.


A useful question structure is: **How does X affect Y in a defined system, place, and period?** Confirm the question, method, permissions, ethics, safety, equipment, and strategy connection with your teacher before extensive data collection. An interesting question is unsuitable if the dependent variable cannot be measured reliably.


### September 15-21: Complete a pilot


A pilot is a small-scale test of your procedure. Take several measurements, trial a survey, or process a sample from the proposed secondary dataset. Check whether the method produces analyzable variation and can be completed within the available time.


Use the results to improve sampling intervals, control variables, categories, instructions, and equipment precision. The[ESS IA step-by-step guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-ess-internal-assessment-step-by-step-guide-for-beginners) provides a practical checklist for questions, methods, data, analysis, and evaluation.


### Late September to Mid-October: Collect Defensible Data


Use **September 22-October 12** as the main collection window. Three weeks allow repeated field visits, laboratory trials, survey responses, or systematic extraction of secondary data. Start promptly if weather, organisms, public access, or participants could disrupt the method.


Prepare raw-data tables before collection. Include units, relevant measurement uncertainty, dates, locations, sampling codes, and qualitative observations that could explain anomalies. Preserve an untouched copy of the original data and document subsequent processing.


Where collaboration is permitted, each submitted investigation must remain individual. Students may sometimes use similar methodologies, but the relevant variable must differ and each student’s qualitative or quantitative data must be unique.


By **October 12** , the evidence should be sufficient to answer the question, not merely produce a graph. If it is inadequate, consult your teacher immediately. Narrowing the question can be more defensible than disguising weak evidence with excessive background information.


### Mid-October to Early November: Process and Analyze


From **October 13-19** , check units and missing values, preserve genuine anomalies, and calculate measures that answer the research question. Depending on the design, these may include means, percentages, diversity indices, rates of change, spread, uncertainty, or an appropriate statistical test.


Choose graphs according to the variables rather than appearance. Include descriptive titles, labeled axes, units, and readable scales. Explain why each processing method is suitable instead of adding complicated statistics merely to appear advanced.


From **October 20-November 2** , identify and quantify patterns, discuss anomalies, and explain possible environmental mechanisms. Distinguish correlation from causation, and consider reliability, validity, bias, and uncertainty where they affect interpretation. Analyze before polishing the introduction so the final report reflects the evidence actually collected.


### November: Draft, Revise, and Submit


### November 3-16: Complete the report


Answer the research question directly using processed results. Indicate how strongly the evidence supports the conclusion and acknowledge conflicting findings. Evaluate specific limitations by explaining their likely effect, then propose feasible improvements. RevisionDojo’s guide to[writing an ESS IA evaluation](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-do-i-write-a-strong-evaluation-in-my-ess-ia-2026-first-assessment) explains how to connect limitations, impacts, and improvements.


Assemble the environmental issue, research question, strategy, perspectives tension, method, data treatment, analysis, conclusion, and evaluation into one coherent report. Remain at or below the official **3,000-word maximum** . Cite borrowed ideas, data, maps, and methods consistently, and keep essential evidence in the report rather than hiding it in appendices.


### November 17-30: Use feedback effectively


Leave at least one week for feedback permitted under your school’s procedures. Address the weakest criteria first, then improve concision, captions, cross-references, formatting, and citations. The[RevisionDojo ESS coursework guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-environmental-systems-and-societies-ess-new-syllabus/coursework-guide) can support a structural audit, while the[ESS IA Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grader/rubric/ess-new-ia) can provide criterion-based indications. Neither replaces teacher guidance or your own judgment.


Aim to submit by **November 28-30** , even if the school deadline is in December. This buffer prevents travel, illness, examinations, or overlapping coursework from turning final checks into emergency work.


### Common Scheduling Mistakes


- **Waiting for the perfect topic:** A focused, feasible investigation is better than an ambitious plan that cannot produce usable data.
- **Skipping the pilot:** Discovering a broken method during main collection can cost weeks.
- **Collecting without a processing plan:** Decide which comparisons, calculations, and graphs the question requires first.
- **Writing analysis too early:** Verify the complete dataset before interpreting it.
- **Ignoring the school calendar:** Holidays, laboratory access, permissions, and feedback dates can alter the schedule.


If you start in October, reduce the scope rather than compressing every stage. Choose accessible data, limit the geographic range, and pilot immediately. The[general IB IA timeline guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-timeline-for-completing-an-ia) can help reorganize the process without removing analysis or revision.


### Conclusion


A reliable **fall IA schedule for ESS** begins in early September, completes data collection by mid-October, and reserves late November for feedback and revision. Weekly deliverables make methodological problems visible while there is still time to correct them.


RevisionDojo can support this schedule through ESS guidance, exemplars, and criterion-based feedback. Use the coursework guide while planning, consult examples for structure, and apply the ESS IA Grader selectively once the complete draft is ready.
